note: Starting a blend-oriented sequence: recover a C3 blend after ethane removal and a C4 blend, while sending C5+ material onward.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a blend-focused light-ends train first (C3, C4, C5, C6 paraffin/naphthene), then add only high-value heavy-product separations if economics permit. Step 1: establish and inspect C3/C4 root split, deethanizer, and C4/C5 split.
Feed has 3300 mol/s and large value in C5/C6 cuts. Blends avoid difficult isomer separations. Initial moderate stages/reflux to gauge purity and expensive-plant costs; light ends kept near feed pressure to limit refrigeration.

note: Use the converged light/C6+ split and add a C4/C5 column to target a sellable C5 blend while avoiding premature heavy-end columns.
notebook:
PLAN: Establish a robust C5/C6+ root split, recover C5 blend from the light stream, then recover C6 blends and test only profitable pure heavy products. Step 1: converge root and C4/C5 split; inspect costs/purities.
My initial high-pressure root failed. R20's 50/3/4/dp0.4 root converges and makes a useful C5-light vs C6+ split. Reuse it and split its tops at 50/3/3/dp0.3; defer C6 processing until revenue and costs are visible.

note: Split the existing C4/C5 stream to recover the high-value C5 blend, with possible pure N-butane overhead.
notebook:
PLAN: Establish a robust C5/C6+ root split, recover C5 blend from the light stream, then recover C6 blends and test only profitable pure heavy products. Step 2: split TB into C4 and C5 blend and establish positive revenue.
The converged root gives TB 843 mol/s with 80% C5 and 19% N-butane. A C4/C5 column should produce a high-value C5 bottoms blend (~$600M/yr) and possibly pure N-butane tops. Use moderate 45 stages and 4/4 at low pressure to avoid excessive cost. Root+T currently cost $353M/yr, so revenue should finally exceed cost if the new split converges.

note: Collapse the light-end train into a single root column with a liquid C5 side draw near the bottom, avoiding two costly columns.
notebook:
PLAN: Replace the uneconomic three-column light-end train with one root column using a liquid side draw for the valuable C5 blend. Then tune draw stage/fraction and separation, and only add further branches if clearly profitable. Step 1: test a single-column C4-/C5/C6+ cut.
The old root+T cost $353M/yr and TB added $69M, while only C5 sold for $407M. A root side draw can potentially retain that revenue with one column. C5s are 695 mol/s =21.1% of feed. Use 60 stages, 4/4, dp0.4 and a liquid draw below feed at stage42. Sell all three outlets; tops/bottoms are intermediate unsold streams for now.

note: Restore the best valid baseline so its exact splits and costs can guide targeted improvements rather than another speculative topology.
notebook:
PLAN: Return to the best converged three-column light-end design, inspect exact stream splits, then improve its economics by reducing column severity/cost and targeting saleable C4/C5/C6 blends. Step 1: restore the -0.035 baseline before making focused changes.
The one-column side-draw root was a failure: no stream approached saleable purity and it still cost $227M/yr. R207 confirms that aggressive tall/high-reflux columns are uneconomic despite $1101M revenue. Best prior design was -0.035 with root+T+TB and C5 blend sales around $407M. Restore it to obtain exact settings and compositions.

note: Copy the best proven island design to establish a profitable baseline before focused cost reductions.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt the island's proven three-column C5/C6 blend flowsheet, establish it as my valid baseline, then reduce the very large root and C6-column costs while preserving blend specifications. Step 1: copy R254 exactly.
R254 earns $1539.1M/yr from C5 and C6-paraffin blends at $1210.5M/yr cost, reward 0.749. Its compact high-boil-up T column is superior to symmetric severe light-end operation. Main opportunities are the $430M root and $518M B column; purity margins are modest, so changes should be incremental.

note: Copy the best island design to bank its substantially lower downstream-column costs before testing further reductions.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt R301's cheaper proven downstream columns, then optimize the dominant $430M root and probe moderate downstream trims without crossing the 95% blend thresholds.
R301 gives reward 0.946 with B=90/9/9 and T=50/5/15; both blends remain sellable. R299 shows B=60/6/6 fails C6 purity, so the feasible boundary is between these. Root settings are unchanged across all good plants and are the next major cost target. Preserve high T boil-up, which is essential to C5 blend quality.

note: Use the proven 60/5/14 light stripper and trim only root stages, retaining its separation duties to avoid the C5 leakage that broke the C6 blend in R348.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt R347's improved light stripper, then cautiously reduce root capital while holding its 6/6 duties; preserve the 90/9/9 C6 splitter, whose purity boundary is sharp.
R347 reaches 0.999 with T=60/5/14, gaining $18.4M revenue and saving $5.2M. R349 shows B=85/8/8 destroys C6 sale; R348 shows root=50/5/5 also destroys it. Current test: root 60/6/6 should cut stages without the duty-driven C5 leakage seen in R348. High T boil-up remains essential.

note: Combine the proven cheaper root with R394's shorter, lower-boil-up light stripper, preserving the sharp C6 split while increasing C5 recovery.
notebook:
PLAN: Combine my cheaper 60-stage root with R394's improved 50/5/13.5 light stripper, retain the essential 90/9/9 C6 splitter, then tune light-stripper boil-up for C5 recovery before considering extra product columns.
R394 earns 1.031: reducing T from 60/5/14 to 50/5/13.5 raises C5 revenue $10.2M and lowers cost $3.6M. My 60/6/6 root gives identical splits to 65 stages and saves $3.2M, so the combination should exceed 1.038. B=88/8.5 fails C6 purity; do not weaken B. TT needs two extra columns for C3/C4 blends and BB needs difficult heavy separations, so focus first on low-risk duty tuning.

note: Apply the proven light-stripper boil-up of 13 to my cheaper 60-stage-root backbone, gaining C5 recovery and lower duty while retaining the sharp C6 split.
notebook:
PLAN: Combine my cheaper 60-stage root with the proven 50-stage light stripper, tune its boil-up downward for C5 recovery, then test incremental savings without weakening the essential C6 splitter.
R442/R445 earn 1.062 at root65 and T=50/5/13: C5 revenue rises $10.4M and T cost falls $3.2M versus 13.5. My root60 preserves splits and costs $3.6M less, so T=13 should give about 1.066. B=88/8.5 previously failed C6 purity; keep B=90/9/9. TT and BB remain unsold; extra columns are expensive, so complete low-risk tuning first.

note: Continue the successful light-stripper boil-up reduction to 11.5 on the cheaper 60-stage root, seeking further C5 recovery before butane leakage begins.
notebook:
PLAN: Continue the proven light-stripper boil-up reduction to maximize C5 recovery, then test small stage/duty savings while preserving the C6 blend split.
My root60/T13 plant scores 1.063. R493 shows root65/T12 scores 1.129, gaining $22.5M revenue and $7M T-column cost versus T13. Root60 saves another $0.4M without changing splits. T11.5 should recover still more C5 and reduce duty; butane breakthrough is the main purity risk. B=90/9/9 is essential: 88/8.5 previously lost C6 purity. BB recovery was uneconomic in R495.

note: Adopt the island-best T11 design and extend its successful boil-up reduction to 10.5, seeking further C5 recovery and lower duty while monitoring butane breakthrough.
notebook:
PLAN: Continue reducing light-stripper boil-up while C5 purity holds, then test modest stage/duty savings on the best backbone.
R542 (root65/T11) scores 1.203: TB grows to 542 mol/s and revenue rises $12.7M while T cost falls $3.9M versus T11.5. No butane leakage is visible. Copy it and test T10.5; root60 saved only $0.4M, so retain root65. B=90/9/9 is essential for C6 purity.

note: Extend the improving light-stripper trend from 10.0 to 9.0 on the cheaper 60-stage root, checking closely for the first butane leakage into the C5 blend.
notebook:
PLAN: Continue reducing light-stripper boil-up while C5 purity holds, then test modest stage/duty savings on the best backbone.

The 10.5→10.0 step gained 16 mol/s C5 and $14M revenue while saving $4.4M cost, so test 9.0 to find the breakthrough point faster. B=90/9/9 remains essential for C6 purity.

notebook:
PLAN: Continue reducing light-stripper boil-up while C5 purity holds, then test modest stage/duty savings on the best backbone.

Root60 is as effective as root65 and slightly cheaper. B=90/9/9 remains essential for C6 purity. Test T8.0 next; stop or reverse if N-butane contaminates TB.

notebook:
PLAN: Continue reducing light-stripper boil-up while C5 purity holds, then test modest stage/duty savings on the best backbone.
Root60/T8.0 scores 1.479: TB 645 mol/s, revenue +$33.9M and T cost -$11.0M versus T9.0, with no butane leakage. Root60 is as effective as root65 and slightly cheaper. B=90/9/9 remains essential for C6 purity. Test T7.0 next; stop or reverse if N-butane contaminates TB. If purity holds, continue toward the recovery optimum before adjusting root or B duties.

note: Reduce the C6 column reflux and boil-up from 9 to 8 while retaining 90 stages, testing whether its already-marginal blend purity survives a substantial duty saving.
notebook:
PLAN: Bank the near-complete C5 recovery at T boil-up 7, then reduce the expensive C6 column duty while preserving its marginal 95% blend purity; afterwards test root savings or T=6.5.
Root60/T7.0 scores 1.542: TB is 688 mol/s and 97% C5, essentially full recovery; further boil-up reduction risks C4 contamination. B=90/9/9 costs $392.6M/yr and BT is only about 95% C6 with 3% N-pentane, so test 90/8/8 first: unchanged stages may retain the split while cutting energy. If purity fails, revert; if it holds, continue cautiously. Root remains 60/6/6/0.5 and T 50/5/7/0.2.

note: Restore the best plant and bracket the narrow C6 purity cliff at 8.5 reflux and boil-up, aiming to retain the blend while recovering part of the energy savings.
notebook:
PLAN: Restore the 1.542 baseline, bracket the C6 column between 8/8 (fails narrowly) and 9/9 (passes), then optimize the successful setting and test root/T savings only if worthwhile.
At B=90/8/8, BT missed C6 purity narrowly and revenue fell $1079M, so this was a purity cliff, not a useful energy saving. Baseline B=90/9/9 gives BT 932 mol/s, ~95% C6, 3% N-pentane and 1% MCP. Test the midpoint 90/8.5/8.5, which should recover much of the ~$41M/yr duty saving if purity holds. T boil-up 7 is optimal: 6 causes 10% butane in TB and loses the blend; 7 gives essentially full C5 recovery. Root 60/6/6/0.5, T 50/5/7/0.2.

note: Adopt the proven four-column plant and trim the C4 splitter from 40 to 35 stages, preserving its comfortable 97% N-butane purity margin while reducing capital cost.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt the profitable 1.752 four-column plant, first trim the small C4 column while retaining >=95% N-butane, then test the highest-value root/C6 savings or a compact C3 recovery column.
R830 adds TT=40/4/5/0.2 to the proven backbone, selling 410 mol/s of 97% N-butane for $146.5M/yr at only $54.6M/yr column cost. A 35-stage version should retain specification with a small capital saving. Keep root 60/6/6/0.5, T 50/5/7/0.2, B 90/9/9/0.1: B 8.5 fails the C6 blend, and T boil-up below 7 causes abrupt C4 leakage into C5. Remaining opportunities: trim TT duties, recover the C3 blend in TTT if net-positive, or cautiously reduce root size.

note: Adopt R878's superior C4-blend split and lower TT boil-up to 2.5, seeking extra C4 recovery and lower duty while retaining blend purity.
notebook:
PLAN: Adopt the profitable C4-blend plant, optimize TT boil-up for recovery and cost, then test only high-value root/C6 savings or compact C3 recovery.
R878 improves reward to 1.808 by using TT=40/4/3/0.2: TTB is a 100% C4 blend worth $172.8M/yr versus $145.6M/yr for pure butane. Its TTB still contains only 504 of 544 feed C4 mol/s, so lowering boil-up to 2.5 may recover more isobutane/butane and reduce duty; monitor overhead C4 contamination and blend purity. Keep root 60/6/6/0.5, T 50/5/7/0.2, B 90/9/9/0.1: B=8.5 or 80/8/8 destroys C6 blend, and T boil-up below 7 causes C4 leakage into C5.

note: Add a small ethane/C3 splitter below TTT: ethane is only 11% of this stream and much more volatile, so a compact column may unlock roughly $220M/yr of C3-blend revenue.
notebook:
PLAN: Add a compact ethane/C3 splitter to monetize TTT, then tune it for sale and cost; afterward test only high-value root/C6 savings.
Current best is 1.825: root 60/6/6/0.5, T 50/5/7/0.2, B 90/9/9/0.1, TT 40/4/2.5/0.2. TTB is a 97% C4 blend worth $178M/yr. TTT contains about 272 mol/s C3 and 34 ethane, so an easy ethane strip can potentially add about $220M/yr C3-blend revenue. Start TTT at 25/2/3/0.1. TT boil-up 2.0 fails C4 purity; 3.0 gives less recovery than 2.5. B below 90/9/9 and T boil-up below 7 destroy blend purity.

note: Cut the deethanizer boil-up sharply: its current overhead rejects about 118 mol/s of valuable C3 with only 34 mol/s ethane, so a much smaller overhead should substantially increase C3 sales and lower duty.
notebook:
PLAN: Tune the new deethanizer to recover nearly all C3 instead of rejecting C3 overhead, then test heavy-end monetization and root/C6 savings.
Best is 1.849 with TTT 25/2/3/0.1. Its bottom is clean C3 but only 154 mol/s; 153 mol/s overhead still contains about 118 mol/s C3. Ethane is only 34 mol/s and highly volatile, so cut reboil from 3 to 0.5 to target a small ethane-rich top and roughly 270 mol/s saleable C3 bottoms. Four-column backbone: root 60/6/6/0.5, T 50/5/7/0.2, B 90/9/9/0.1, TT 40/4/2.5/0.2. TT boil-up 2.0 destroys C4 blend; B below 90/9/9 and T boil-up below 7 destroy blend purity. R967 shows TT can use 30 stages with negligible cost change.

note: Test two easy heavy-end splits for premium n-octane while applying the proven small TT and B capital savings; the octane product could add about $400M revenue.
notebook:
PLAN: Finish low-cost light-end tuning, then monetize BB with a two-column octane recovery train; retain only changes that beat 1.946.
Current deethanizer 25/2/0.5/0.1 sells 260 mol/s C3 for $65.5M at only $12.2M cost; overhead loses about 19 mol/s C3 and ethane purification is not worthwhile. Trim TT to 30 and B to 88 using proven neutral savings. Test BB 40/3/3 to split heptane and lighter overhead from octane/nonane bottoms, then BBB 30/3/3 to recover premium n-octane overhead. Root 60/6/6/0.5, T 50/5/7/0.2 and B 88/9/9/0.1 preserve blend purity; B below 9 reflux/boil and T boil-up below 7 fail. TT boil-up 2.0 fails. R1008's B side draw destroys more paraffin value than it unlocks.

note: Restore the island-best backbone and correct the heavy-end separation sequence: BB now targets a sharp heptane/octane cut, allowing BBB to recover octane and nonane rather than leaving an unsellable octane/nonane mixture.
notebook:
PLAN: Restore the 1.947 five-column backbone, then test a two-column heavy-end train that makes BB a sharp heptane/octane split and BBB an octane/nonane splitter; retain only profitable purity.
Heavy-end train at 40/3/3 and 30/3/3 lost $118M without sales. Its key flaw was wrong cuts: BBB bottoms contained 24% nonane, so heptane/octane splitting can never yield pure octane. BB must instead reject all heptane overhead; BBB then splits octane overhead from nonane bottoms. Potential sales are about $463M/yr. Root/T/TT/TTT settings are proven. T boil-up below 7 and B reflux/boil below 9 fail; TTT boil-up 0.5 is essential to C3 blend purity. B88 and TT30 are small safe savings but R1040 is marginally best.

note: Restore the best backbone and test a stronger BB boil-up to expel heptane overhead; a following 50-stage C8/C9 splitter should then recover premium octane without the failed naphthene branch.
notebook:
PLAN: Restore R1071 (best 1.955), then shift BB from a naphthene/heptane cut to a heptane/octane cut by raising boil-up; add an octane/nonane splitter only if BBB becomes suitably binary.
R1071's TTT boil-up 0.35 is worth +0.009 over 0.5 and retains C3 sales. Heavy tests failed because the original BB 80/8/8 leaves 31% heptane in BBB; subsequent octane/nonane recovery is impossible there. Raising BB boil-up to 12 should drive heptane overhead, leaving mainly C8/C9 below. Potential C8+C9 sales are about $463M/yr. B reflux/boil below 9 destroys C6 blend; T boil-up below 7 fails. Keep all other proven settings unchanged.

note: Restore the best five-column plant and test root reflux 5.8 plus the proven 88-stage C6 column, targeting small cost reductions without changing the separation sequence.
notebook:
PLAN: Abandon the unprofitable heavy-end branch, restore R1126 (2.001), then make small verified capital/energy trims to root and B while retaining all blend purities.
Heavy recovery did not pay: even the successful octane recovery in R1129 left overall reward only 1.735. R1126 proves root reflux 5.9 is safe and improves reward to 2.001. B at 88 stages is safe and slightly cheaper. Current test combines root 5.8 with B88; if purity holds, cautiously continue root trim. T boil-up below 7 and B reflux/boil below 9 are known failure cliffs.

notebook:

Root reflux 5.8 improved both revenue and cost, giving 2.047; B88 is safe. Test 5.75 as the last root trial because a full downstream re-solve leaves only four solves. B reflux/boil below 9 and T boil-up below 7 are known failure cliffs. Heavy-end recovery did not pay.

note: Adopt the proven 2.093 backbone and test one final C6-column stage reduction from 88 to 87, seeking a small capital saving while retaining the C6 blend.
notebook:
